Alex.confusing: Nothing major, though how hugs and confusion interact with night reports, and whether a Floofer hug on a Farm player would show up, was unclear to me.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when I was Meowfia and pushed the table to eggsecute Blair, a Farm player, with a Hawk claim. It worked and won the round.
Alex.change: Give Meowfia some way to learn about each other, or a stronger night action. Round 2 had two Meowfia who couldn't coordinate, and Ellis and I both claimed Hawk.
Alex.regret: In round 3 as Tit I guessed Ellis was Hawk with no real reason. I should have visited a quieter player, or picked a role more likely to give information. I also threw my Wild and a 7 when I could have kept more cards.

Blair.confusing: How the Owl's report and egg counts interact with other visitors. In round 2 I got +0 and wasn't sure what that implied, and my explanation sounded shaky.
Blair.fun: Round 1: my Eagle report exposed Casey and the table converged on her fast. Round 3's deduction from the Owl's visitor list was also satisfying.
Blair.change: I'd make the Owl and Eagle reports clearer about whether an Owl's own visit counts as a visitor, since that confusion cost me round 2.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed "Blair, Owl" but told the table nobody visited me, which contradicted Finley's list and got me eggsecuted. I should have said I didn't know who visited me, since an Owl's report only covers its target, and not thrown at Finley.

Casey.confusing: How a thrown card banks only if your team wins, so throwing small amounts as a loser returns just one card. It was also unclear how Hawk and Pigeon claims could be cross-checked when roles are not unique.
Casey.fun: Round 2, calling out the duplicate Hawk claims as the real Hawk and watching Alex and Ellis, the two actual Meowfia, scramble. Seeing the table's logic fall apart on Blair was entertaining too.
Casey.change: Give the loser's consolation more value, or let Meowfia learn at least one teammate. As it is, a Meowfia player who is caught early has almost no way back, and I ended the game far behind.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I falsely claimed Pigeon and said I visited Drew, which the egg counts disproved and got me eggsecuted. I would have claimed a role that left no checkable trail, such as Kookaburra, or at least not named a specific visit target.

Drew.confusing: How the Floofer's hug interacts with visits, and whether hugged roles still report truthfully; also how the Eagle's count was supposed to reconcile with Owl eggs in round 2.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when the table converged on Casey and my 12 banked for 14 points; also spotting Blair's contradiction in round 2.
Drew.change: Give Meowfia some way to coordinate, or give the Tit a way to learn something even on a miss, so that guessing blind feels less random.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I falsely claimed Kookaburra, which Ellis's Owl list and Finley's real claim exposed at once. I should have claimed a vague role like Pigeon, or a Hawk who visited a quiet player, and not named a role that was easy to check.

Ellis.confusing: How the Owl and Kookaburra reports interact with confusion and what counts as a "visit". Also the round 2 egg math, where Finley's +4 versus Blair's Owl visit was hard to reconcile.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 as the Mouser. I bluffed as a Hawk next to a real Hawk, then steered the vote onto a Farm player, and Meowfia won.
Ellis.change: Tell players the Meowfia count, or give Meowfia a way to find each other. Fake claims like my second Hawk are too easy to get away with, and a lone Meowfia has little to work with.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I claimed Hawk after Alex had already claimed it, which put me under suspicion for no reason. I should have claimed a role nobody had taken, such as Falcon or Kookaburra, so the table couldn't catch me copying.

Finley.confusing: Nothing major. The one unclear point was how Owl and Eagle egg counts interact with other visitors, which I had to work out mid-day.
Finley.fun: Round 1, when my Hawk hit on Casey, we found the Meowfia fast, and I banked all six cards, 44 points, in one throw.
Finley.change: Let the dealt hands and round-one winnings matter less. The round 1 scores made a runaway lead too easy to hold, and a Farm win was worth far more than anything else.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I threw five cards at Blair and pushed the early CAW. Blair was Farm, and the real Meowfia (Alex and Ellis) were both Hawk claimants. I should have pressed the double Hawk claim before ending the day, and thrown fewer cards.

review.title: Wrong Egg, Right Lead
review.headline: Meowfia won one round by steering the table onto an innocent Owl.
review.summary: Round 1 ended fast: a lone Sphinx lied about her visit and the table piled on her. Round 2 was the one real puzzle. Two Meowfia and a Hawk all claimed Hawk, and the table voted out the honest Owl after she botched her wording. Round 3 repeated round 1: Drew was caught lying about his role and the Farm voted him out. Ellis won at 72 by staying a quiet, safe vote-follower on the winning side.

rounds.recap: Casey, a lone Meowfia Sphinx, claimed Pigeon and said she visited Drew. Drew's nest showed no egg, so the lie was provable. Finley's Hawk egg and Blair's Eagle visitor list backed it up. Casey was voted out unanimously and Farm won.

Everyone visited Blair, the Owl, who was hugged by the Floofer. Finley the Eagle saw four visitors. Alex (Floofer) and Ellis (Mouser) both fake-claimed Hawk, as did the real Hawk, Casey. Blair said nobody visited her, which contradicted the Eagle's list. Farm piled onto her and the Meowfia won.

Ellis the Owl got the visitor list at Alex: Floofer, Hawk, Kookaburra. Blair and Finley owned the Hawk and Kookaburra slots. Drew's fake Kookaburra claim failed against Finley's real one. He admitted the lie and was voted out. Casey the Sphinx was suspected but survived.

highlights.text: Casey's invented Pigeon visit to Drew fell apart at once, because Drew's +0 count disproved it.
Three players claimed Hawk. The table saw the contradiction but never used it, and voted for Blair's sloppy wording instead.
Alex and Ellis, both Meowfia and not knowing each other, each saw the Blair vote was good for them and quietly joined the pile-on.
Blair worked out from Ellis's Owl list that the only slot left for the Floofer was Drew, and the table then agreed.

confusions.what: She said nobody visited her. She was the Owl and learns nothing about visitors, and she was hugged. She later called it a misspeak.

He said an Owl visiting him would have given him +5. The Owl lays an egg only if nobody else visited, so the claim was muddled. Blair, the Owl, visited him alongside no one but she saw others at Blair, not at him.
He said an Owl at Finley would have made him +5. The Owl lays an egg only when no one else visited, so this was a wrong reading of the Owl.
She said her Hawk report was garbled by Blair being visited. Hawk reports are not affected by that.
He guessed Hawk on Ellis, who was Owl. The Tit guess was random, which is not a rules error but wasted the action.
He said a Kookaburra not visited proves no one visited him. That is true, but he also overlooked that a Floofer hug could still hide a visit's effect.

worked: Egg counts as evidence: Drew's +0 killed Casey's Pigeon claim in round 1. Finley's +4 revealed everyone's visit in round 2.
Owl visitor-animal lists plus unique-animal claims let Farm solve round 3 by elimination. This was a fair deduction puzzle.
Several people claiming the same one-copy animal (Hawk in round 2) made a real, readable contradiction.
Throw-count scoring made Meowfia think about the consolation card. Casey and Drew threw only their top card at a Farm player.
problems: Round 2: nothing forced the table to resolve the triple Hawk claim. They voted on Blair's slip instead. The Eagle's visitor list showed the Meowfia visits, but nobody asked who was missing from it.
Most night choices are random, so round 1 and round 3 night actions gave little info. Round 1 was a solved lone-Meowfia round by the first beat.
The Floofer hug zeroed out Blair's Owl and wasted her report. Round 2's result hinged on that, so the hug may be too strong. Consider giving the hugged player a notice.
Standings barely mattered. Casey and Drew were out of the running early, and the leaders just threw high cards at the consensus target. Third-round tension was low.
Rules text is hard to apply. The Owl's egg condition and the Hawk/Tit effects were misread repeatedly. A short summary card for each animal's reporting would help.
